summary: Mobile-only frontend test of Statements Depth (StatementDetail dark-aware + Downloads & records, Audit Log, Compare) on Expo web preview. All new testIDs are present, gating rules (has_original_file / isPdf) work, navigation to Compare and Audit Log is correct, and both light+dark themes render with high-contrast, legible text. BUG: the three download buttons (Decoded CSV, Decoded PDF, Download original) all fail on the Expo web preview and surface the error text 'Couldn't download the decoded ... Please try again.' — this violates the explicit requirement that on the web preview the download must not crash / no error text on success.

ui_bugs.issue: Tapping Decoded CSV / Decoded PDF / Download original on the Expo web preview throws (expo-file-system/legacy downloadAsync + cacheDirectory are not usable in the browser) and renders the error text 'Couldn't download the decoded CSV/PDF/original file. Please try again.' The requirement says the flow must not crash and no error text should appear on success on the web preview. Reference: /app/mobile/src/lib/download.ts:16 (uses cacheDirectory + downloadAsync unconditionally) and /app/mobile/app/statement/[id].tsx:73-91 (runDownload catches and sets dlError). Same code path is reused by /app/mobile/app/statement-compare/[id].tsx:47-59 (Open original file).

integration_issues.issue: downloadAndShare() in /app/mobile/src/lib/download.ts calls expo-file-system/legacy downloadAsync against `${cacheDirectory}<file>`. On web `cacheDirectory` is not a real writable location and downloadAsync is not supported — the promise rejects, runDownload's catch fires, and the UI shows the 'Couldn't download…' message. Suggested fix: branch on Platform.OS === 'web' and use a fetch()+blob()+anchor.click() download (or window.open with a signed URL) so the web preview succeeds silently while native keeps the share sheet.

issues: Verified visually in dark theme: high-contrast text on dark bg, sage AI insight card still legible, orange/terracotta accents on primary CTAs remain readable, audit timeline event titles and dates are clear. No contrast issues found.

action_items: Fix mobile web download flow in /app/mobile/src/lib/download.ts so that on Platform.OS === 'web' the code does NOT call expo-file-system/legacy (which throws on web). Recommended: on web, do a fetch() with the Authorization + X-Participant-Id headers, convert to a Blob, and trigger a temporary <a download> click; on native keep the current cacheDirectory + Sharing.shareAsync path. Also swallow/hide dlError on web when the browser fallback succeeds.
Consider migrating off expo-file-system/legacy to the current expo-file-system API in a follow-up; the /legacy subpath is on a deprecation path.
critical_code_review_comments: /app/mobile/src/lib/download.ts is platform-agnostic but the APIs it uses (cacheDirectory, downloadAsync from expo-file-system/legacy) are effectively native-only — the code silently breaks on Expo web preview which is the ONLY runtime our reviewers can screenshot.
runDownload() in /app/mobile/app/statement/[id].tsx surfaces the same generic error string regardless of the underlying failure — consider logging the caught error to console for easier RCA.

rca of the issue: Downloads: /app/mobile/src/lib/download.ts imports { cacheDirectory, downloadAsync } from 'expo-file-system/legacy'. On the Expo web preview these are native-shim placeholders — cacheDirectory is null/undefined and downloadAsync rejects because there is no native file-system bridge. The promise rejection propagates to runDownload's catch in statement/[id].tsx (and openOriginal in statement-compare/[id].tsx), which sets dlError and renders the 'Couldn't download…' text under the buttons. Reproduction: log in as cathy@example.com, open /statement/dd6fd5bb-89b7-40f7-855c-3510837b0410, scroll to 'Downloads & records', tap 'Decoded CSV' — the error text appears within ~2s. Mitigation: in download.ts, wrap the native path with `if (Platform.OS !== 'web') { …native cacheDirectory+downloadAsync+Sharing… } else { const res = await fetch(url,{headers}); const blob = await res.blob(); const a = document.createElement('a'); a.href = URL.createObjectURL(blob); a.download = filename; a.click(); URL.revokeObjectURL(a.href); }` so the browser downloads directly and no error text is shown.
